For a simple one-to-one equilibrium a lower dissociation constant (KD, a concentration often given in nanomolar units) means tighter binding, whereas papers that report association constants (per molar) read the other way, with a higher value meaning tighter binding, so compare like with like.

proofs.sourceScope: Ways and Parham measured association constants in a named antibody/cell system. The KD direction is a simple one-to-one model definition, not an empirical optimum.

proofs.requirement: Multivalent apparent cell binding is not automatically single-site affinity; target density, spacing and assay preparation matter.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Avidity is the combined strength of several contacts and depends on target density, spacing and the number of binding sites. In one set of experiments the Fab fragment of an anti-HLA-A2 antibody had an affinity of 1.9 x 10^7 per molar while the bivalent F(ab)2 or IgG showed an avidity of 1.3 x 10^9 per molar on cells (Ways and Parham, 1983). A cell-binding result for a multivalent product is therefore not its single-site affinity; ask which assay was used and how many sites took part.

proofs.sourceScope: The model distinguishes intrinsic one-site interaction from observed multivalent binding. Target density, spacing and preparation are assay-reading qualifications, not a universal numerical correction.

proofs.requirement: Stability, aggregation and unwanted recognition/developability need separate tests from affinity.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Developability asks whether a molecule can be produced, purified, formulated and stored, stays soluble and stable, does not aggregate and does not bind unrelated molecules.

Stability is read from thermal unfolding and aggregation, which depend on formulation, concentration and stress. A potency assay shows activity in that assay only. FDA Q6B ties specifications to the individual product, so no universal developability cutoff exists, and tests consume candidate material and may need target protein or cells.

proofs.sourceScope: Jain measured a dozen biophysical properties on matched IgG1 preparations from 137 clinical-stage antibody sequences. Q6B separates characterization dimensions. No optimal threshold or clinical validation is inferred.

proofs.requirement: A stronger measured interaction does not establish better delivery or a safer or more effective treatment; no universal optimum is depicted.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: In mice bearing SK-OV-3 human ovarian carcinoma xenografts, four affinity variants of one anti-HER2 antibody that recognise the same epitope (monovalent KD 270 to 0.56 nmol/L) showed the highest tumour accumulation at moderate affinity; the highest-affinity antibodies stayed in the perivascular space (average penetration 20.4 um versus 84.8 um for the lowest affinity), a conditional result in that model, not an ideal affinity (Rudnick et al., 2011).
Neither study tests whether a candidate works or is safe in patients, so developable does not mean effective or safe.

proofs.sourceScope: The Rudnick abstract and two selected complete body paragraphs give a conditional comparison in scid mice with SK-OV-3 xenografts. The biodistribution protocol used 20 micrograms intravenously; the tissue-distance analysis used 500 micrograms intraperitoneally. These are distinct readouts and protocols, not a transferable affinity optimum or patient-treatment ranking.

proofs.requirement: In the fictional A/B example 1 nM is tighter than 10 nM in the same assay, while different aggregation and native-cell evidence do not select a treatment.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Affinity describes one binding interaction under stated conditions. For a simple one-to-one equilibrium a lower dissociation constant (KD, a concentration often given in nanomolar units) means tighter binding, whereas papers that report association constants (per molar) read the other way, with a higher value meaning tighter binding, so compare like with like.

Inference lesson. Suppose candidate A has tighter single-site affinity but only purified-protein data and more aggregation after stress, while candidate B binds living target-positive cells and aggregates less. No treatment choice follows: the team needs the intended format, comparable functional tests and exposure evidence first. A binder profile is a development framework, not a validated score, and it is retested once the binder becomes an antibody, a payload carrier or a receptor.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Definitions. A conventional antibody pairs heavy- and light-chain variable domains to form a binding site. A single-chain variable fragment (scFv) joins those two domains with a peptide linker in one polypeptide chain, so single-chain does not mean one variable domain (Huston et al., 1988, a 15-amino-acid linker).

proofs.sourceScope: Huston reports linked VH/VL, one chain and a tested anti-digoxin construct. A linked chain can contain two domains; no universal success for every linker is claimed.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: VHH is the binding domain of a camelid heavy-chain-only antibody (Hamers-Casterman et al., 1993), and an isolated VHH used as a binder is called a nanobody (Bathula et al., 2021).

evidence.supportingExcerpt: A receptor-bearing cell, its genetic instructions and its receptor protein are different objects.
A common CAR presents a binder outside the cell and signaling domains inside it, connected through a spacer and transmembrane region.
Fab, the arm with the binding site, and Fc, the stem, are separate parts: binding does not guarantee killing, and Fc effector contacts need compatible effector cells or complement.

proofs.requirement: Linked domains must fold and recover actual binding in the tested construct; architecture alone does not show every linker or sequence works.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: The original single-chain Fv work linked antibody heavy- and light-chain variable regions and tested binding after expression and refolding. Camelid heavy-chain antibody studies established a different architecture without light chains, underlying VHH-derived formats. More recent engineered-cell comparisons test the behavior of particular fragments in particular constructs. Format names describe architecture; they do not by themselves establish stability, specificity or therapeutic superiority.

The first single-chain Fv joined the heavy- and light-chain variable domains of an anti-digoxin antibody with a 15-amino-acid linker (relative molecular mass 26,354); after refolding it showed digoxin specificity like the Fab and an association constant (3.2 x 10^7 per molar) about six-fold below the Fab's (Huston et al., 1988).

proofs.sourceScope: Huston tested a particular engineered and renatured anti-digoxin sFv. Its recovery of specificity and changed association constant do not validate every sequence, linker or final format.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Sources and depth. The three older papers were read at abstract level only; Watson et al. A computational design counts as a binder only after it is made and measured: in Watson et al. 95 designs per target were screened at 10 micromolar and only designs at or above half the control's maximal response counted, so most tested designs did not meet that criterion, and ranking scores are predictions.

Each result is a measured interaction under stated laboratory conditions. A selected, enriched or designed sequence is a candidate; the studies do not test activity in cells in a patient, absence of binding to healthy tissue, or clinical benefit.
